content.bodyUz:
Multilevel Speaking Part 1 — «tanishuv» qismi: ish/o'qish, uy, kundalik hayot, sevimli mashg'ulot haqida oddiy savollar. Ko'pchilik buni «oson» deb o'ylab, bir og'iz javob beradi va shu yerda ball yo'qotadi.

Aslida imtihonchi Part 1 da uchta narsani tekshiradi:
1. **Ravonlik** — javob to'xtovsiz oqadimi yoki har so'zdan keyin o'ylab qolasizmi?
2. **Kengaytirish qobiliyati** — savolga javob berib, o'zingiz qo'shimcha ma'lumot bera olasizmi?
3. **Tabiiylik** — jonli, og'zaki ingliz tili yoki yodlangan yozma matnmi?

Eng muhimi: **Part 1 da javobingiz yodlangan insho kabi yangramasligi kerak.** Qisqartmalar (I'm, don't, I'd), «to be honest», «actually», «I mean» kabi so'zlashuv belgilari — bular XATO emas, aynan C1 belgisi.

turns.speaker: Examiner
turns.en: Do you work, or are you a student?
turns.uz: Siz ishlaysizmi yoki talabamisiz?

turns.speaker: You
turns.en: I'm a student at the moment — I'm in my third year, studying translation. To be honest, I ended up there almost by accident: I'd originally planned to do law, but I'd always been the kid who watched films without subtitles, so translation just felt like a more natural fit. What I enjoy most is the practical side of it. We do live interpreting sessions every Friday, and there's nothing quite like the panic of hearing a sentence you don't fully understand and having to produce something sensible anyway.
turns.uz: Hozircha talabaman — uchinchi kursdaman, tarjimashunoslik yo'nalishida o'qiyman. Rostini aytsam, bu yerga deyarli tasodifan tushib qoldim: dastlab yuridik yo'nalishni rejalashtirgandim, lekin men doim filmlarni subtitrsiz ko'radigan bola bo'lganman, shu sababli tarjima menga tabiiyroq tuyuldi. Eng yoqadigan jihati — amaliy tomoni. Har juma kuni jonli tarjima mashg'ulotlari bo'ladi, va to'liq tushunmagan gapingizni eshitib, baribir mazmunli narsa aytishga majbur bo'lish hissiga teng keladigani yo'q.

content.titleUz: P-R-E-E ramkasi: har qanday Part 1 savoliga javob
content.bodyUz:
Har bir Part 1 javobini shu to'rt qadamda quring:

**P — Position (Fikr):** savolga TO'G'RIDAN-TO'G'RI javob bering. *Yes, definitely. / Not really, no. / I'm a student at the moment.*

**R — Reason (Sabab):** nima uchun? *mainly because... / the main reason is that...*

**E — Example (Misol):** bitta konkret misol. *For instance, last week... / Take yesterday, for example...*

**E — Extension (Kengaytma):** yon tomonga bir qadam — kelajak, taqqoslash yoki kichik hazil. *Although I have to say... / That said, ...*

Agar javobingizda to'rttasi ham bo'lsa, uzunligi avtomatik 40-70 so'z chiqadi — bu Part 1 uchun ideal. **Ko'proq gapirmang:** Part 1 da 90 so'zdan oshsa, imtihonchi sizni to'xtatadi va bu ham yaxshi taassurot emas.

items.en: P: I'm a student at the moment — I'm in my third year, studying translation.
items.uz: Fikr: to'g'ridan-to'g'ri javob, hech qanday aylanma yo'q.

items.en: R: I'd originally planned to do law, but ... translation just felt like a more natural fit.
items.uz: Sabab: shaxsiy va ishonarli. «Because it is interesting» emas.

items.en: E: We do live interpreting sessions every Friday.
items.uz: Misol: konkret kun, konkret faoliyat. Imtihonchi buni eshitib «rost gapiryapti» deb his qiladi.

items.en: E: there's nothing quite like the panic of hearing a sentence you don't fully understand
items.uz: Kengaytma: his-tuyg'u qo'shildi. Javob shu yerda «tirik» bo'ldi.

content.bodyUz: Eng keng tarqalgan C1 tuzog'i: javobni haddan tashqari «chiroyli» qilishga urinish. Agar siz «Furthermore, it should be noted that...» desangiz, bu Part 1 da G'ALATI yangraydi — bu yozma til. Og'zaki C1 = murakkab fikr + oddiy, tabiiy ohang. Qisqartmalardan qo'rqmang: **I'm, don't, I'd, there's** — bularsiz nutqingiz robot kabi eshitiladi.

content.bodyUz:
Ish va o'qish — Part 1 ning ENG ehtimolli mavzusi. Deyarli har bir imtihonda uchraydi, chunki imtihonchi shu yerdan sizni «ochadi».

Tuzoq: bu mavzu sizga tanish bo'lgani uchun ko'pchilik AVTOMATIK, yodlangan javob beradi — «I am a student. I study economics. It is very interesting.» Bu B1 darajasi.

C1 farqi — **konkretlik**. Umumiy gap emas, aniq detal: qaysi kun, qaysi predmet, necha soat, qanday his. Quyidagi 6 ta transkriptni ovoz chiqarib takrorlang: maqsad ularni yodlash emas, ohangni va tuzilishni his qilish.

turns.speaker: Examiner
turns.en: What do you enjoy most about your studies?
turns.uz: O'qishingizda sizga eng ko'p nima yoqadi?

turns.speaker: You
turns.en: Probably the fact that it's never the same two days running. One day we're doing dry grammar analysis, and the next we're sitting in a booth trying to interpret a speech in real time. I thrive on that kind of variety, honestly. If I had a job where I did exactly the same thing every morning, I think I'd lose my mind within a month.
turns.uz: Ehtimol, ikki kun ketma-ket bir xil bo'lmasligi. Bir kuni quruq grammatik tahlil qilamiz, ertasi kuni kabinada o'tirib nutqni jonli tarjima qilishga urinamiz. Rostini aytsam, men shunday xilma-xillikdan kuch olaman. Agar har kuni ertalab aynan bir xil ish qiladigan ishim bo'lsa, bir oyda aqldan ozardim deb o'ylayman.

turns.speaker: Examiner
turns.en: Is there anything you'd like to change about your working day?
turns.uz: Ish kuningizda o'zgartirmoqchi bo'lgan narsa bormi?

turns.speaker: You
turns.en: Yeah, the commute, without a doubt. I lose nearly two hours a day on buses, and there's no way to make that time useful — it's too crowded to read properly. If I could change one thing, it'd be working from home two days a week. I'm fairly sure I'd get more done, although I might miss the office chat more than I'd like to admit.
turns.uz: Ha, shubhasiz, yo'lda o'tadigan vaqt. Kuniga qariyb ikki soatni avtobuslarda yo'qotaman va bu vaqtni foydali qilishning iloji yo'q — to'g'ri o'qish uchun juda gavjum. Bitta narsani o'zgartira olsam, haftasiga ikki kun uydan ishlash bo'lardi. Ko'proq ish bajarardim deb ancha ishonaman, garchi ofisdagi suhbatlarni tan olishni istaganimdan ko'proq sog'inishim mumkin.

turns.speaker: Examiner
turns.en: How do you usually spend your mornings?
turns.uz: Odatda ertalablaringizni qanday o'tkazasiz?

turns.speaker: You
turns.en: My mornings are pretty hectic, to be honest. I'm up at half six, and from then on it's basically back-to-back until I leave the house — coffee, checking messages, a very rushed breakfast. I keep telling myself I'll start getting up earlier so I can actually ease into the day, but so far that's remained more of an aspiration than a habit.
turns.uz: Rostini aytsam, ertalablarim ancha shiddatli. Olti yarimda turaman va uydan chiqqunimcha hamma narsa ketma-ket — qahva, xabarlarni ko'rish, juda shosha-pisha nonushta. O'zimga «ertaroq turishni boshlayman, kunga sekin kiraman» deb aytaveraman, lekin hozircha bu odatdan ko'ra ko'proq orzu bo'lib qolyapti.

items.en: it's never the same two days running
items.uz: «two days running» = ketma-ket ikki kun. Tabiiy og'zaki kolokatsiya, darslikda kam uchraydi — shuning uchun kuchli taassurot qoldiradi.

items.en: I thrive on that kind of variety
items.uz: «thrive on» — C1 fe'l birikmasi: biror narsadan kuch olmoq. «I like variety» dan ancha yuqori daraja.

items.en: I think I'd lose my mind within a month
items.uz: Ikkinchi turdagi shart gap + kichik mubolag'a. Grammatika va shaxsiylik bir vaqtda — imtihonchi tabassum qiladi, siz ball olasiz.

items.en: without a doubt
items.uz: Fikrni kuchaytiruvchi qisqa ibora. Javob boshida ishonch bildiradi va sizga bir soniya o'ylash beradi.

items.en: If I could change one thing, it'd be...
items.uz: Tayyor ramka. «O'zgartirmoqchimisiz?» tipidagi HAR QANDAY savolga moslashadi — yodlab oling.

items.en: more than I'd like to admit
items.uz: O'zini ustidan yengil kulish. Bunday nuans B1/B2 javobda deyarli uchramaydi.

items.en: pretty hectic
items.uz: «hectic» = shiddatli, tig'iz. «Very busy» ning C1 muqobili; «pretty» esa uni yumshatadi.

items.en: it's basically back-to-back
items.uz: «back-to-back» = tanaffussiz, ketma-ket. Ish/o'qish mavzusida oltin ibora.

items.en: that's remained more of an aspiration than a habit
items.uz: «more of an X than a Y» konstruksiyasi — nozik taqqoslash. Bu bitta gap javobni B2 dan C1 ga ko'taradi.

content.titleUz: 4-6 namunalar: kun tartibi va mehnat madaniyati

turns.speaker: Examiner
turns.en: Do you prefer to plan your day or just take it as it comes?
turns.uz: Kuningizni rejalashtirishni afzal ko'rasizmi yoki qanday kelsa shundaymi?

turns.speaker: You
turns.en: I'm somewhere in the middle, I'd say. I always write a rough list in the morning — three things I genuinely have to finish — but I've learnt not to plan every hour, because something always comes up. My sister is the opposite: she colour-codes her entire week. It works brilliantly for her, but I'd find it exhausting.
turns.uz: Aytardimki, men o'rtada turaman. Ertalab har doim taxminiy ro'yxat yozaman — chindan tugatishim shart bo'lgan uchta ish — lekin har soatni rejalashtirmaslikni o'rgandim, chunki doim kutilmagan narsa chiqadi. Opam buning aksi: butun haftasini rangli belgilar bilan taqsimlaydi. Unga ajoyib to'g'ri keladi, menga esa charchatarli tuyulardi.

turns.speaker: Examiner
turns.en: How has your daily routine changed in the last few years?
turns.uz: So'nggi bir necha yilda kundalik tartibingiz qanday o'zgardi?

turns.speaker: You
turns.en: It's changed quite dramatically, actually. A few years ago my whole day revolved around a timetable someone else had set — school bells, basically. Now I have far more control, which sounds great, but it also means nobody's chasing me if I waste a morning. I've had to build my own structure from scratch, and that took me a good year to get right.
turns.uz: Rostdan ham ancha keskin o'zgardi. Bir necha yil oldin butun kunim boshqa birov tuzgan jadval atrofida aylanardi — asosan maktab qo'ng'irog'i. Endi menda ancha ko'p nazorat bor, bu yaxshi eshitiladi, lekin ayni paytda ertalabni behuda o'tkazsam, hech kim meni ta'qib qilmaydi. O'z tartibimni noldan qurishga to'g'ri keldi va uni to'g'rilash menga bir yilcha vaqt oldi.

turns.speaker: Examiner
turns.en: Do you think people in your country work too much?
turns.uz: Sizningcha, mamlakatingizda odamlar haddan tashqari ko'p ishlaydimi?

turns.speaker: You
turns.en: Some do, definitely — especially people running their own small businesses. My uncle has a car parts shop and he's there from eight in the morning until eight at night, six days a week. Having said that, I don't think it's the same everywhere. A lot of my friends in offices finish at six and genuinely switch off. So it probably depends far more on the sector than on the country.
turns.uz: Ba'zilar, albatta — ayniqsa o'z kichik biznesini yuritayotganlar. Amakimning avto ehtiyot qismlari do'koni bor, u haftasiga olti kun ertalab sakkizdan kechqurun sakkizgacha o'sha yerda. Shunga qaramay, hamma joyda ham shunday emas deb o'ylayman. Ofisda ishlaydigan ko'p do'stlarim oltida tugatadi va chindan ham ishdan uziladi. Shuning uchun bu mamlakatdan ko'ra ko'proq sohaga bog'liq bo'lsa kerak.

items.en: I'm somewhere in the middle, I'd say.
items.uz: «Ikkisidan qaysi biri?» savoliga eng yaxshi C1 javobi — qat'iy tanlamay, nuans bering. Bu fikrlash chuqurligini ko'rsatadi.

items.en: I've learnt not to plan every hour, because something always comes up.
items.uz: Present Perfect + «come up» frazali fe'li. Tajriba orqali o'rganganingizni bildiradi — bu shaxsiylik ballini oshiradi.

items.en: she colour-codes her entire week
items.uz: Konkret, jonli detal. Imtihonchi buni eshitib sizning javobingiz haqiqiy ekaniga ishonadi.

items.en: It's changed quite dramatically, actually.
items.uz: «dramatically» + «quite» — kuchaytiruvchi va yumshatuvchi birga. Bu og'zaki C1 ning tipik balansi.

items.en: my whole day revolved around a timetable someone else had set
items.uz: «revolve around» kolokatsiyasi + Past Perfect nisbiy gapda. Bitta gapda ikkita yuqori daraja belgisi.

items.en: nobody's chasing me if I waste a morning
items.uz: Present Continuous majoziy ma'noda + shart gap. Tirik, so'zlashuv sintaksisi.

items.en: Having said that, ...
items.uz: Konsessiya (qarshi fikrni tan olish) belgisi. Part 1 da ham, Part 3 da ham ishlaydi — universal C1 quroli.

items.en: genuinely switch off
items.uz: «switch off» = ishdan aqlan uzilmoq. Kundalik hayot mavzusida idiomatik va tabiiy.

items.en: it probably depends far more on the sector than on the country
items.uz: «far more ... than ...» qiyosiy kuchaytirish + xulosa. Javobni professional tarzda yopadi.

content.bodyUz: Bu 6 ta javobni yodlab olmang — YODLANGAN javob imtihonchiga darhol bilinadi (ohang tekislashadi, ko'z aloqasi yo'qoladi). Buning o'rniga har bir javobdan **2-3 ta iborani** oling va o'z hayotingiz haqidagi gapga joylang. Masalan: «I thrive on...» + o'zingizning haqiqiy sababingiz. Shunda til C1 bo'ladi, mazmun esa sizniki bo'ladi.

content.bodyUz:
Sevimli mashg'ulot, texnologiya va sayohat — Part 1 ning eng tez-tez uchraydigan uchligi. Sababi oddiy: har bir insonda ular haqida aytadigan gap bor.

Ayni shu «hammaga tanish» xususiyat tuzoq ham: o'quvchilar shu mavzuda eng klishe javoblarni beradi — *«I like reading books. Books are very useful.»*

C1 javobning siri — **kutilmagan konkretlik**. «I like reading» emas, «I'm halfway through a book about the history of the Silk Road and I keep falling asleep on page forty». Ikkinchisi eslab qolinadi, birinchisi esa yuzta boshqa javob bilan aralashib ketadi.

Quyidagi 6 ta transkriptda shu konkretlikni qanday yaratish ko'rsatilgan.

turns.speaker: Examiner
turns.en: What do you do to relax?
turns.uz: Dam olish uchun nima qilasiz?

turns.speaker: You
turns.en: My go-to is cycling, actually. There's a route along the canal near my flat and I do maybe twenty kilometres on a Sunday morning, usually with no music, which surprises people. I find that after about ten minutes my brain finally stops running through my to-do list. It's the one hour in the week where I'm genuinely not thinking about anything.
turns.uz: Aslida, mening asosiy vositam — velosipedda yurish. Kvartiram yonidagi kanal bo'ylab marshrut bor va yakshanba tongida taxminan yigirma kilometr yuraman, odatda musiqasiz, bu odamlarni ajablantiradi. Sezishimcha, o'n daqiqadan keyin miyam nihoyat rejalar ro'yxatini takrorlashni to'xtatadi. Bu haftada chindan ham hech narsa haqida o'ylamaydigan yagona soatim.

turns.speaker: Examiner
turns.en: Have you taken up any new hobbies recently?
turns.uz: Yaqinda biror yangi mashg'ulot boshladingizmi?

turns.speaker: You
turns.en: I have, yeah — I started learning the piano about eight months ago, which was completely out of the blue. A neighbour was moving abroad and more or less gave me his old keyboard. I'm still terrible, I should say. I can play about one and a half songs. But there's something quite satisfying about being genuinely bad at something as an adult — you forget what that feels like.
turns.uz: Ha, boshladim — sakkiz oycha oldin pianino o'rganishni boshladim, bu mutlaqo kutilmaganda bo'ldi. Qo'shnim chet elga ko'chib ketayotgan edi va eski klavishasini menga deyarli sovg'a qildi. Aytishim kerak, hali ham juda yomon chalaman. Bir yarim qo'shiq chala olaman. Lekin katta yoshda biror narsani chindan yomon bajarishda qandaydir mamnuniyat bor — bu his qanaqaligini unutib qo'yasan.

turns.speaker: Examiner
turns.en: How much time do you spend on your phone?
turns.uz: Telefoningizga qancha vaqt sarflaysiz?

turns.speaker: You
turns.en: Far too much, and I know the exact number because the phone helpfully tells me — about four and a half hours a day. In my defence, a good chunk of that is podcasts while I'm walking. But the rest? Scrolling, mostly. I've tried those app blockers a couple of times and I lasted, I think, three days before I deleted them.
turns.uz: Haddan tashqari ko'p, va aniq raqamni bilaman, chunki telefonning o'zi «xayrixohlik bilan» aytib turadi — kuniga to'rt yarim soatcha. O'zimni oqlab aytsam, buning katta qismi yurganimda eshitadigan podkastlar. Qolgani-chi? Asosan varaqlash. O'sha ilova bloklovchilarini bir-ikki marta sinab ko'rdim va o'chirib tashlashimdan oldin, o'ylashimcha, uch kun chidadim.

items.en: My go-to is cycling
items.uz: «go-to» = doim murojaat qiladigan, asosiy tanlov. Zamonaviy, tabiiy og'zaki ibora — darslikda deyarli yo'q.

items.en: which surprises people
items.uz: Butun gapga tegishli nisbiy gap (sentential relative). C1 sintaksisining aniq belgisi.

items.en: my brain finally stops running through my to-do list
items.uz: Majoziy tasvir. Umumiy «I relax» o'rniga jonli manzara — imtihonchi buni eslab qoladi.

items.en: I started learning the piano ... which was completely out of the blue
items.uz: «out of the blue» = kutilmaganda. Idioma to'g'ri kontekstda ishlatilgan — bu Lexical Resource ning eng yuqori bandi.

items.en: more or less gave me his old keyboard
items.uz: «more or less» — yumshatuvchi. Aniq bo'lmagan holatni tabiiy tarzda ifodalaydi.

items.en: I'm still terrible, I should say.
items.uz: O'zini kamsitib aytish (self-deprecation) + «I should say» qo'shimchasi. Bu ingliz og'zaki nutqining madaniy belgisi.

items.en: Far too much, and I know the exact number
items.uz: Kutilmagan halollik + aniq raqam va'dasi. Javobni darhol qiziqarli qiladi.

items.en: In my defence, ...
items.uz: «O'zimni oqlab aytsam» — yengil hazil ohangidagi ramka. Nutqni tirik qiladi.

items.uz: Gap o'rtasida «I think» bilan to'xtash. Bu real og'zaki nutq ritmi — yodlangan matnda hech qachon bo'lmaydi.

turns.speaker: Examiner
turns.en: Do you think technology has made life easier or more stressful?
turns.uz: Sizningcha, texnologiya hayotni osonlashtirdimi yoki ko'proq tashvishli qildimi?

turns.speaker: You
turns.en: Both, and I don't think that's a cop-out answer. Practically, it's easier — I can pay a bill in forty seconds instead of standing in a queue. But the same phone that saves me those forty seconds also means my boss can reach me at ten at night. So the tasks got easier and the boundaries got worse, if that makes sense.
turns.uz: Ikkalasi ham, va menimcha bu javobdan qochish emas. Amaliy jihatdan osonroq — navbatda turish o'rniga to'lovni qirq soniyada amalga oshiraman. Lekin menga o'sha qirq soniyani tejaydigan telefon ayni paytda rahbarim menga kechqurun soat o'nda ham yeta olishini anglatadi. Ya'ni vazifalar osonlashdi, chegaralar esa yomonlashdi, agar tushunarli bo'lsa.

turns.speaker: Examiner
turns.en: Do you prefer travelling alone or with other people?
turns.uz: Yolg'iz sayohat qilishni afzal ko'rasizmi yoki boshqalar bilanmi?

turns.speaker: You
turns.en: It really depends on the trip, I find. For a city break I'd rather go alone — I can change my mind ten times a day and nobody complains. But for anything longer than a week, I'd want company, because after a while you start wanting to say «look at that» to someone. I went to Bukhara on my own two summers ago and by day five I was talking to the hotel cat.
turns.uz: Sezishimcha, bu chindan sayohat turiga bog'liq. Shahar bo'ylab qisqa sayohat uchun yolg'iz borishni afzal ko'rardim — kuniga o'n marta fikrimni o'zgartirsam ham hech kim norozi bo'lmaydi. Lekin bir haftadan uzoqroq narsa uchun hamroh xohlardim, chunki bir muddatdan keyin kimgadir «anavini qara» deb aytging kela boshlaydi. Ikki yoz oldin Buxoroga yolg'iz borgandim va beshinchi kuni mehmonxona mushugi bilan gaplashayotgandim.

turns.speaker: Examiner
turns.en: Is there anywhere in your country you'd recommend to a visitor?
turns.uz: Mamlakatingizda mehmonga tavsiya qiladigan joyingiz bormi?

turns.speaker: You
turns.en: Everyone says Samarkand, and they're right, but I'd push people towards Nurata, honestly. It's much smaller, there's a mountain spring with fish that supposedly nobody's allowed to catch, and you can stay in a yurt about an hour further out. The point is you actually talk to people there. In the big cities you can spend three days and only ever speak to waiters.
turns.uz: Hamma Samarqand deydi va ular haq, lekin rostini aytsam, men odamlarni Nurata tomon undardim. U ancha kichik, u yerda baliqlari bor tog' buloqi bor — aytishlaricha, ularni hech kim tutolmaydi — va bir soatcha narida yurtada tunashingiz mumkin. Gap shundaki, u yerda odamlar bilan chindan gaplashasiz. Katta shaharlarda uch kun o'tkazib, faqat ofitsiantlar bilan gaplashishingiz mumkin.

items.en: Both, and I don't think that's a cop-out answer.
items.uz: «cop-out» = javobdan qochish. O'z javobingizni oldindan himoya qilish — juda tabiiy og'zaki harakat.

items.en: the same phone that saves me those forty seconds also means...
items.uz: Bitta obyektning ikki tomonini bir gapda ko'rsatish. Bu «murakkab fikr» belgisi va Part 3 ga ham tayyorlaydi.

items.en: the tasks got easier and the boundaries got worse
items.uz: Parallel qurilish (parallelism). Qisqa, esda qoladigan, professional yakun.

items.en: if that makes sense
items.uz: Tinglovchi bilan aloqa. Bu «hedge» sizni tabiiy va o'ziga ishongan qilib ko'rsatadi.

items.en: It really depends on the trip, I find.
items.uz: «I find» — «mening tajribamda». Fikrni shaxsiylashtiruvchi qisqa ibora.

items.en: I'd rather go alone
items.uz: «would rather» konstruksiyasi — afzallik bildirishning C1 shakli. «I prefer» dan ko'ra og'zakiroq.

items.en: by day five I was talking to the hotel cat
items.uz: Kutilmagan, kulgili konkret detal. Bu javobni butun imtihon davomida eslab qolinadigan qiladi.

items.en: I'd push people towards Nurata
items.uz: «push someone towards» — jonli fe'l birikmasi. «I recommend» dan ancha tabiiyroq.

items.en: that supposedly nobody's allowed to catch
items.uz: «supposedly» = aytishlaricha. Ma'lumot manbaiga masofa qo'yish — nozik C1 harakati.

items.en: The point is you actually talk to people there.
items.uz: «The point is...» — asosiy fikrni ajratib ko'rsatish. Javobni tarqalib ketishdan saqlaydi.

content.titleUz: Nega qisqa javob eng katta yo'qotish?
content.bodyUz:
Part 1 taxminan 4-5 daqiqa davom etadi. Agar har savolga 5 so'z bilan javob bersangiz, imtihonchida sizni baholash uchun MATERIAL qolmaydi.

Baholovchi shunday o'ylaydi: «Men bu odamning murakkab grammatikani ishlata olishini bilmayman, chunki u umuman ishlatmadi.» Natijada u OLDINGI, past darajani belgilaydi. Bu jazolash emas — bu dalil yetishmasligi.

Muhim nuqta: kengaytirish **imtihonchi qo'shimcha savol berishini kutmasdan** amalga oshiriladi. C1 nomzod savol berilishini kutmaydi — o'zi ochib beradi.

Javobingiz tugab qolganini his qilsangiz, shu to'rttadan birini qo'llang:

**1. SABAB (Why?)** — *mainly because... / the thing is, ...*
**2. MISOL (When exactly?)** — *Take last Tuesday, for instance... / Just yesterday...*
**3. TAQQOSLASH (Compared to what?)** — *whereas my brother... / it wasn't like that five years ago...*
**4. KELAJAK yoki FARAZ (What next?)** — *I'm hoping to... / if I had more time, I'd...*

Qoida: har javobda kamida IKKITASINI ishlating. Ikkitasi javobni avtomatik 40+ so'zga olib chiqadi va grammatik xilma-xillikni ta'minlaydi (o'tgan zamon + shart gap + kelasi zamon bir javobda).

For a child, definitely — there's space, everyone knows everyone, and my mum never worried where I was. For a teenager, less so. By sixteen most of my friends were desperate to leave, myself included.

content.bodyUz:
Sizga kartochka beriladi: mavzu va 2-3 ta yo'naltiruvchi savol. Odatda bu **taqqoslash** tipidagi topshiriq: «Ba'zilar X ni afzal ko'radi, boshqalar Y ni. Sizningcha qaysi biri yaxshiroq?»

Tayyorgarlik: taxminan **1 daqiqa**. Gapirish: **2 daqiqa**.

Ikki daqiqa juda uzun tuyuladi. Amalda esa aksincha bo'ladi: strukturasiz gapirsangiz, 40 soniyada aytadigan gapingiz tugaydi va qolgan vaqtni jimlik yoki takror bilan to'ldirasiz.

**Yechim — arxitektura.** Nima aytishni emas, QANDAY TARTIBDA aytishni oldindan biling. Shunda ikki daqiqa o'z-o'zidan to'ladi.

**1. KIRISH (10-15 soniya)** — savolni o'z so'zingiz bilan qayta ayting va nima qilishingizni e'lon qiling.
*«Right, so this is one of those questions where I can see both sides — let me take them in turn.»*

**2. BIRINCHI TOMON (30-35 soniya)** — bitta fikr + bitta KONKRET misol.
*«Starting with X — the obvious advantage is... My cousin, for example, ...»*

**3. IKKINCHI TOMON (30-35 soniya)** — qarshi tomon + yana bitta konkret misol.
*«On the other hand — and this is the part people underestimate — ...»*

**4. SHAXSIY TANLOV + YAKUN (25-30 soniya)** — o'z pozitsiyangizni aniq ayting va nuans bilan yoping.
*«If I had to come down on one side, I'd probably... Having said that, ask me again in ten years...»*

Jami: 100-115 soniya. Qolgan vaqt tabiiy pauzalarga ketadi.

When I worked on a group project last year, a classmate spotted an error in my calculations that I'd read past about six times. On the other hand — and this is what people forget — teams are slow. Every decision needs a meeting, and half the meeting is people repeating each other. If I had to come down on one side, I'd say it depends on the stage of the work: alone for the thinking, together for the checking. Having said that, I'm probably biased, because I've always found it easier to concentrate in an empty room.

turns.uz: Ba'zilar katta shaharda yashashni afzal ko'radi, boshqalar esa kichik shaharchani. Sizningcha qaysi biri yaxshiroq? Tayyorgarlik uchun bir daqiqa, gapirish uchun ikki daqiqa.

turns.speaker: You
turns.en:
Right, so this is one of those questions where I can genuinely see both sides, so let me take them in turn.

Starting with big cities — the obvious advantage is opportunity. If you want a particular job, a particular course, even a particular kind of restaurant, a city is where you'll find it. My cousin moved to Tashkent three years ago for a job in IT that simply didn't exist in our town, and within eighteen months he'd been promoted twice. That kind of thing just doesn't happen in a place with one employer.

On the other hand — and this is the part people underestimate — cities charge you for that opportunity. Not just in rent, although the rent is brutal, but in time. He spends around two hours a day commuting, which works out at something like twenty days a year sitting on a bus. In a small town you'd be at work in ten minutes.

If I had to come down on one side, I'd probably choose the city, at least for now. I'm at a stage where I need options more than I need peace and quiet, and I think it's easier to move from a city to a town later than the other way round.

Having said that, ask me again in fifteen years, and I suspect I'll be the one talking about clean air and knowing my neighbours.
turns.uz:
Xo'sh, bu — men chindan ikkala tomonni ham ko'ra oladigan savollardan biri, shuning uchun ularni birma-bir olay.

Katta shaharlardan boshlaymiz — ravshan afzallik bu imkoniyat. Agar sizga muayyan ish, muayyan kurs, hatto muayyan turdagi restoran kerak bo'lsa, uni shahardan topasiz. Amakivachcham uch yil oldin Toshkentga bizning shaharchamizda umuman mavjud bo'lmagan IT ishi uchun ko'chib ketdi va o'n sakkiz oy ichida ikki marta lavozimi ko'tarildi. Bitta ish beruvchisi bor joyda bunday narsa shunchaki bo'lmaydi.

Boshqa tomondan — va odamlar aynan shu jihatni past baholaydi — shaharlar bu imkoniyat uchun sizdan haq oladi. Faqat ijara bilan emas, garchi ijara shafqatsiz bo'lsa-da, balki vaqt bilan. U kuniga ikki soatcha yo'lda o'tkazadi, bu yiliga yigirma kunni avtobusda o'tirish demakdir. Kichik shaharchada esa ishga o'n daqiqada yetib borgan bo'lardingiz.

Bir tomonni tanlashim kerak bo'lsa, hech bo'lmasa hozircha, ehtimol shaharni tanlardim. Men shunday bosqichdamanki, menga tinchlikdan ko'ra imkoniyatlar ko'proq kerak, va menimcha shahardan shaharchaga keyinroq ko'chish, aksincha qilishdan osonroq.

Shunga qaramay, o'n besh yildan keyin yana so'rang — o'shanda toza havo va qo'shnilarni tanish haqida gapirayotgan men bo'lsam kerak.

**Kirish (2 gap, ~14 so'z)** — 12 soniya.
**Birinchi tomon (4 gap, ~75 so'z)** — 38 soniya.
**Ikkinchi tomon (4 gap, ~62 so'z)** — 33 soniya.
**Shaxsiy tanlov (2 gap, ~50 so'z)** — 27 soniya.
**Yakun (1 gap, ~22 so'z)** — 12 soniya.

Jami: ~223 so'z, ~122 soniya. Tezlik: **daqiqasiga ~110 so'z** — bu tabiiy, shoshilmagan og'zaki tezlik.

**Muhim xulosa:** ikki daqiqani to'ldirish uchun sizga 220 so'z kerak — bu atigi 13-14 gap. Har tomonga 4 ta gap. Bu sonni yodda tuting: **tomoniga 4 gap.** Ko'p emas, kam ham emas.

Tezlikni sinash mashqi: shu transkriptni telefoningizda ovozga yozib oling va davomiyligini qarang.

- **1:50 - 2:10** — mana bu C1 tezligi.

Bu mashqni haftada uch marta, har safar boshqa matn bilan bajaring. Bir oyda tezlik hissi avtomatlashadi.

content.bodyUz:
Ko'pchilik nomzod 60 soniyada **to'liq gaplar yozishga** urinadi. Bu ikki tomondan halokatli:

1. **Ulgurmaysiz.** Bir daqiqada 3-4 gapdan ortiq yoza olmaysiz — monolog uchun 13 gap kerak.
2. **O'qib berasiz.** Yozilgan gap ko'z oldingizda tursa, siz uni gapirmaysiz, O'QIYSIZ. Imtihonchi buni ohangdan darhol biladi: ritm tekislashadi, pauzalar noto'g'ri joyda bo'ladi, ko'z aloqasi yo'qoladi. Bu Fluency ballini tushiradi.

**To'g'ri yondashuv:** gap emas, **skelet** yozing. 10-12 ta so'z va belgi — hammasi shu. Qolganini og'zingiz o'sha payt yaratadi va aynan shu narsa tabiiy yangraydi.

**0-10 soniya — TANLOV.** Qaysi tomonni oxirida tanlashingizni HOZIROQ hal qiling. Bu eng muhim 10 soniya: agar oxirigacha ikkilanib gapirsangiz, monolog yo'nalishsiz bo'ladi.

**10-30 soniya — IKKI USTUN.** Varaqni ikkiga bo'ling. Chap ustunga 1-tomon uchun 2 ta belgi, o'ng ustunga 2-tomon uchun 2 ta belgi.

**30-50 soniya — MISOLLAR.** Eng qiyin va eng qimmatli qism. Har ustunga bitta KONKRET narsa yozing: odam nomi, joy, raqam. Faqat bitta so'z yetarli — «cousin/IT», «bus 2h».

**50-60 soniya — YAKUN.** Oxirgi jumlangizni belgilang: qaysi tomonni tanlaysiz va qanday nuans bilan yopasiz. Bitta belgi: «city ✓ / 15yr?»

Hammasi. Ko'proq yozmang.

content.bodyUz:
Bitta namunani ko'rgan o'quvchi odatda uni **yodlab olishga** harakat qiladi. Ikkita namunani yonma-yon ko'rgan o'quvchi esa boshqacha narsani ko'radi: **mavzu butunlay boshqa, lekin skelet aynan bir xil.**

Mana shu tushuncha kursdagi eng qimmatli narsa. Chunki imtihonda sizga qaysi mavzu tushishini hech kim bilmaydi — lekin ARXITEKTURA doim bir xil bo'ladi.

Quyidagi monologda o'sha to'rt qism bor: kirish + reja, birinchi tomon misol bilan, ikkinchi tomon misol bilan, shaxsiy tanlov va nuansli yakun. Faqat mazmun almashgan.

turns.speaker: Examiner
turns.en: Some people believe children should start learning a foreign language at primary school, while others think it is better to wait until secondary school. Which do you think is better? You have one minute to prepare and two minutes to speak.
turns.uz: Ba'zilar bolalar chet tilini boshlang'ich sinfdan boshlashi kerak deb hisoblaydi, boshqalar esa o'rta maktabgacha kutish yaxshiroq deydi. Sizningcha qaysi biri yaxshiroq? Bir daqiqa tayyorgarlik, ikki daqiqa gapirish.

turns.speaker: You
turns.en:
OK, so — when children should start a foreign language. I'll take the early-start argument first, then the case for waiting, and then say where I land.

The argument for starting young is mostly about pronunciation, as far as I understand it. Young children pick up sounds almost without noticing, whereas by the time you're fifteen you're filtering everything through your first language. My niece started English at six, and her accent is noticeably better than mine — and I've been studying for years longer than she has.

The counter-argument, though, is a practical one rather than a linguistic one. Primary schools in a lot of places simply don't have specialists. You end up with a class teacher who learned the language at university and hasn't used it since. Two years of that can actually put children off, and putting a child off a subject at seven is quite hard to undo.

Where I land, personally, is that the age matters far less than the teacher. I'd rather a child started at eleven with someone who genuinely speaks the language than at six with someone reading from a textbook.

And if I'm being completely honest, the thing that made the difference for me wasn't school at all — it was subtitles and a stubborn refusal to read them.
turns.uz:
Xo'sh — bolalar chet tilini qachon boshlashi kerak. Avval erta boshlash argumentini, keyin kutish tarafdorlarining dalilini olaman, so'ng qayerda turishimni aytaman.

Erta boshlash tarafidagi dalil, tushunishimcha, asosan talaffuzga oid. Kichkina bolalar tovushlarni deyarli sezmasdan o'zlashtiradi, o'n besh yoshga borganingizda esa hamma narsani ona tilingiz orqali filtrlaysiz. Jiyanim ingliz tilini olti yoshda boshlagan va uning talaffuzi menikidan sezilarli darajada yaxshi — men esa undan bir necha yil ko'proq o'qiganman.

Qarshi dalil esa lingvistik emas, ko'proq amaliy. Ko'p joylarda boshlang'ich maktablarda mutaxassis yo'q. Natijada tilni universitetda o'rgangan va o'shandan beri ishlatmagan sinf rahbari bilan qolasiz. Ikki yil shunday o'qish bolani fandan sovutishi mumkin, yetti yoshda sovigan bolani qaytarish esa ancha qiyin.

Mening shaxsiy xulosam shuki, yosh o'qituvchidan ancha kam ahamiyatga ega. Bola olti yoshda darslikdan o'qiydigan kishi bilan boshlagandan ko'ra, o'n bir yoshda tilni chindan biladigan kishi bilan boshlaganini afzal ko'rardim.

Va rostini aytsam, menga farq qildirgan narsa umuman maktab emas edi — u subtitrlar va ularni o'qishdan qaysarlik bilan bosh tortish edi.

content.titleUz: Yakunni qanday qilib esda qolarli qilish
content.bodyUz:
Har ikkala monolog ham **kutilmagan shaxsiy detal** bilan tugadi:

- «ask me again in fifteen years, and I suspect I'll be the one talking about clean air»
- «it was subtitles and a stubborn refusal to read them»

Bu tasodif emas. Imtihonchi kuniga o'nlab javob eshitadi va ularning aksariyati bir xil tugaydi: *«So, in conclusion, I think both have advantages and disadvantages.»* Bu jumla hech qanday ball keltirmaydi.

**Yakun uchun uchta ishonchli usul:**
1. **Kelajakka ishora:** *Ask me again in ten years...*
2. **O'zini yengil masxara:** *Although I say that as someone who...*
3. **Kutilmagan haqiqiy detal:** *Honestly, the thing that changed it for me was...*

Har uchalasi ham javobni SIZNIKI qiladi — va aynan shu narsa yodda qoladi.

Ko'chirish mashqi (eng samarali usul): Monolog #2 ning skeletini oling va uni butunlay boshqa mavzuga to'ldiring.

Masalan, «Ba'zilar mashinada, boshqalar jamoat transportida yurishni afzal ko'radi»:
- *«OK, so — how people should get around town. I'll take the car argument first, then the case for public transport...»*
- *«The argument for driving is mostly about flexibility, as far as I can tell...»*
- *«The counter-argument, though, is an economic one rather than a practical one...»*
- *«Where I land, personally, is that...»*

Skelet o'zgarmadi, mazmun butunlay yangi. Shu mashqni 5 ta turli mavzuda bajaring — shundan keyin arxitektura sizga o'ylashsiz keladi.

content.bodyUz:
Part 3 da imtihonchi Part 2 mavzusini **abstrakt darajaga** ko'taradi. Savollar endi siz haqingizda emas — jamiyat, tendensiya va g'oyalar haqida:

- *«Do you think governments should fund the arts?»*
- *«Why do some people find it hard to change their habits?»*
- *«Will traditional shops disappear completely?»*

Uch muhim farq:
1. **«I» kamayadi, «people / society / most of us» ko'payadi.**
2. **Javob uzunroq:** 60-90 soniya (Part 1 da 30 soniya edi).
3. **Fikringiz asoslanishi shart:** dalil, misol yoki sabab bo'lmasa, javob bo'sh hisoblanadi.

Eng katta xato — savolni shaxsiy savol sifatida tushunish. *«Do you think governments should fund the arts?»* savoliga *«Yes, I like museums»* deb javob berish — mavzudan chiqib ketish.

Part 3 javobining eng ishonchli tuzilishi:

**P — Position (Pozitsiya, ~10 soniya).** Fikringizni darhol ayting, lekin yumshatgich bilan.
*«On balance, I'd say yes — though with a fairly big condition attached.»*

**A — Argument (Dalil, ~25 soniya).** Nima uchun? Mexanizmni tushuntiring: sabab va natija zanjiri.
*«The reasoning is fairly simple: X leads to Y, and Y in turn means...»*

**C — Counter (Qarshi tomon, ~25 soniya).** Qarshi fikrni tan oling va javob bering.
*«Now, the obvious objection is that... And there's something in that. But...»*

**E — Evaluation (Baholash, ~15 soniya).** Xulosa: sharoit, chegara yoki kelajak.
*«So it probably comes down to how it's done rather than whether it's done at all.»*

Jami: 70-80 soniya. Bu Part 3 uchun ideal uzunlik.

turns.speaker: Examiner
turns.en: Do you think governments should spend public money on the arts, or should that money go to more practical areas like healthcare?
turns.uz: Sizningcha, hukumatlar davlat mablag'ini san'atga sarflashi kerakmi yoki bu pul sog'liqni saqlash kabi amaliyroq sohalarga ketishi kerakmi?

turns.speaker: You
turns.en:
On balance I'd say yes, they should — though with a fairly big condition attached, which I'll come back to.

The reasoning, for me, is that the arts aren't really a luxury item, they're a kind of infrastructure. A city with a decent theatre and a couple of galleries keeps its young people for longer, and it attracts the sort of visitors who stay for three days instead of three hours. Take Bilbao, for instance — one museum genuinely changed the economics of an entire city.

Now, the obvious objection is that when a hospital is short of equipment, spending on a gallery looks almost offensive, and honestly, there's something in that. I wouldn't defend an expensive opera house in a town without a functioning clinic.

But I'd say the two budgets aren't really competing in the way people assume — arts funding is usually a rounding error next to healthcare. Cutting it entirely wouldn't buy you a hospital; it would just close the gallery.

So where I end up is that it isn't really a question of whether, but of proportion — and that's a much less exciting argument, unfortunately.
turns.uz:
Umuman olganda ha, sarflashi kerak derdim — garchi ancha jiddiy bir shart bilan, unga qaytaman.

Mening dalilim shuki, san'at aslida hashamat emas, u bir turdagi infratuzilma. Yaxshi teatri va bir-ikki galereyasi bor shahar yoshlarini uzoqroq ushlab qoladi va uch soat emas, uch kun qoladigan mehmonlarni jalb qiladi. Masalan, Bilbaoni oling — bitta muzey butun shaharning iqtisodini chindan o'zgartirdi.

Endi, ravshan e'tiroz shuki, kasalxonada uskuna yetishmayotganda galereyaga pul sarflash deyarli haqoratomuz ko'rinadi va rostini aytsam, bunda jon bor. Ishlaydigan poliklinikasi yo'q shaharda qimmat opera teatrini himoya qilmagan bo'lardim.

Lekin men aytardimki, bu ikki byudjet odamlar o'ylagandek raqobatlashmaydi — san'atga ajratiladigan mablag' sog'liqni saqlash yonida odatda arzimas qism. Uni butunlay qisqartirish sizga kasalxona olib bermaydi; u shunchaki galereyani yopadi.

Shunday qilib, mening xulosam: gap «kerakmi yoki yo'qmi» da emas, balki nisbatda — va afsuski, bu ancha kamroq qiziqarli bahs.

content.titleUz: Nega qarshi fikrni tan olish sizni kuchli qiladi?
content.bodyUz:
Ko'p o'quvchi shunday o'ylaydi: «Agar qarshi fikrni tan olsam, imtihonchi mening fikrim zaif deb o'ylaydi.» Bu **butunlay noto'g'ri**.

Baholovchi uchun manzara boshqacha:
- Faqat bitta tomonni ko'rgan nomzod = mavzuni yuzaki tushungan.
- Ikki tomonni ko'rib, keyin ham o'z pozitsiyasini saqlagan nomzod = mavzuni chuqur tushungan.

**Muhim shart:** konsessiya YAKKA holda ishlamaydi. U doim juftlikda keladi:

**KONSESSIYA (tan olish) + REBUTTAL (rad etish yoki cheklash)**

Agar faqat tan olsangiz, o'z fikringizdan voz kechgan bo'lasiz. Agar faqat rad etsangiz, o'jar ko'rinasiz. Ikkalasi birga — ana shu C1.

Qarshi fikrni tan olgandan keyin uchta yo'ldan birini tanlang:

**1. MIQYOSNI CHEKLASH** — qarshi fikr to'g'ri, lekin faqat tor doirada.
*«That's certainly true of large cities. Outside them, though, the picture is completely different.»*

**2. AHAMIYATNI KAMAYTIRISH** — qarshi fikr to'g'ri, lekin unchalik muhim emas.
*«That's a fair point, but it's a fairly small cost compared with what you get back.»*

**3. SABABNI QAYTA IZOHLASH** — qarshi fikrdagi hodisa to'g'ri, lekin sababi boshqa.
*«I'd agree that's happening — I'm just not convinced technology is what's causing it.»*

Uchtasi ham «You're wrong» demasdan pozitsiyangizni saqlaydi. Ingliz munozara madaniyatida aynan shu yumshoq qat'iylik yuqori baholanadi.

turns.speaker: Examiner
turns.en: Some people say social media has made young people less able to communicate face to face. Would you agree?
turns.uz: Ba'zilar ijtimoiy tarmoqlar yoshlarning yuzma-yuz muloqot qilish qobiliyatini pasaytirdi deydi. Rozimisiz?

turns.speaker: You
turns.en:
Partly, yes — but I think the claim is usually made far too broadly.

The obvious counter-argument to my scepticism is the one everybody's seen: a table of teenagers in a cafe, all on their phones, nobody speaking. And there's a lot in that, honestly. I've been at that table. Something has clearly shifted in how comfortable people are with silence, or with small talk with a stranger.

Where I'd push back, though, is on the assumption that the skill has disappeared rather than moved. My younger brother is hopeless at phoning a shop — genuinely dreads it — but he can hold a conversation with forty people in a group chat, manage a disagreement in it, and defuse an argument. That's a communication skill. It just isn't the one my parents recognise as one.

So I'd say both things can be true at once: face-to-face confidence has probably dropped, while a different set of skills has developed in parallel. Whether that's a net loss really depends on what the next twenty years of work look like.

Qisman ha — lekin menimcha bu da'vo odatda haddan tashqari keng aytiladi.

Mening shubhamga qarshi ravshan dalil — hamma ko'rgan manzara: kafedagi stol atrofida o'smirlar, hammasi telefonida, hech kim gapirmaydi. Va rostini aytsam, bunda jon ko'p. Men ham o'sha stolda o'tirganman. Odamlarning sukunat bilan yoki notanish kishi bilan yengil suhbat bilan qanchalik erkin ekanida nimadir aniq o'zgardi.

Lekin men e'tiroz bildiradigan joyim — bu ko'nikma ko'chgan emas, YO'QOLGAN degan taxmin. Ukam do'konga qo'ng'iroq qilishga umuman yaramaydi — chindan qo'rqadi — lekin u guruh chatida qirq kishi bilan suhbat olib bora oladi, undagi kelishmovchilikni boshqara oladi va janjalni bostira oladi. Bu ham muloqot ko'nikmasi. Faqat u ota-onam ko'nikma deb tan oladigan turi emas.

Shuning uchun ikkala fikr ham bir vaqtda to'g'ri bo'lishi mumkin derdim: yuzma-yuz ishonch, ehtimol, pasaygan, ayni paytda boshqa ko'nikmalar to'plami parallel rivojlangan. Bu umumiy yo'qotishmi yoki yo'qmi — keyingi yigirma yilda ish qanday ko'rinishiga bog'liq.

content.bodyUz:
Part 3 da eng ko'p ball yo'qotiladigan joy: nomzod aqlli fikr aytadi, keyin uni **isbotlamaydi** va boshqa aqlli fikrga o'tadi. Natijada javob umumiy va bo'sh chiqadi.

Qoida oddiy: **har bir umumiy fikrdan keyin 10 soniya ichida konkret narsa ayting.** Konkret narsa uch xil bo'ladi:

1. **MISOL** — real hodisa, joy, odam. *Take Bilbao, for instance...*
2. **DALIL** — tadqiqot, statistika, tendensiya. *There's fairly good evidence that...*
3. **TAJRIBA** — shaxsiy kuzatuv. *I've noticed with my own students that...*

Uchtasi ham ishlaydi. Eng kuchli javoblarda ikkitasi ketma-ket keladi: umumiy dalil + shaxsiy misol.

Imtihonda hech kim sizdan aniq raqamlarni yodlashingizni kutmaydi. Aslida **noto'g'ri raqam aytish xavflidir**, chunki uydirma ekani sezilib qoladi.

Yechim — **himoyalangan murojaat** (hedged reference). Dalilga ishora qiling, lekin aniqlikni da'vo qilmang:

- *«There's fairly good evidence that...»* (manba nomlanmaydi)
- *«I read somewhere that... though don't quote me on the exact figure.»*
- *«Studies on this tend to show that...»*
- *«The figure I remember was something like a third, but the direction matters more than the number.»*

Oxirgi ibora ayniqsa kuchli: siz raqamning aniq emasligini tan olasiz, lekin argumentingizni saqlaysiz. Bu **halollik + ishonch** — imtihonchi buni juda yuqori baholaydi.

**Xavfli variant:** *«Scientists proved that 87% of people...»* — bunday aniq da'vo tekshirib bo'lmaydi va sun'iy yangraydi.

turns.speaker: Examiner
turns.en: Why do you think it is so difficult for people to change their habits, even when they know a habit is harmful?
turns.uz: Sizningcha, odat zararli ekanini bilsalar ham, odamlar uchun odatni o'zgartirish nega shunchalik qiyin?

turns.speaker: You
turns.en:
I think the honest answer is that knowing something and feeling it are two completely different systems, and only one of them is in charge at eleven at night.

There's fairly good evidence that habits are mostly triggered by context rather than by decisions — the same chair, the same time of day, the same walk past the same shop. Studies on this tend to show that people who move house have a much easier time dropping an old habit, which is a strange finding until you think about it. Don't quote me on the exact figures, but the direction is pretty consistent.

Take smoking, for instance. Almost nobody who smokes is unaware of the risk — the warning is literally printed on the packet in enormous letters. So information clearly isn't the missing piece. What seems to work far better is changing the surroundings: a different route home, a different set of friends on a Friday.

I've noticed the same thing with my own studying, actually. Willpower did nothing for me. Leaving the house did.

Which suggests, at least, that we probably blame people for weak character when the real problem is that we've asked them to fight their own kitchen.
turns.uz:
Menimcha, halol javob shuki, bilish va his qilish — butunlay ikki xil tizim, va kechqurun soat o'n birda ulardan faqat bittasi boshqaradi.

Odatlar asosan qarorlar bilan emas, kontekst bilan qo'zg'atilishi haqida ancha yaxshi dalillar bor — o'sha stul, kunning o'sha vaqti, o'sha do'kon yonidan o'sha yurish. Bu boradagi tadqiqotlar odatda shuni ko'rsatadiki, uy o'zgartirgan odamlar eski odatdan ancha oson voz kechadi — o'ylab ko'rmaguningizcha bu g'alati natija. Aniq raqamlar uchun meni kafil qilmang, lekin yo'nalish ancha barqaror.

Masalan, chekishni oling. Chekadiganlarning deyarli hech biri xavfdan bexabar emas — ogohlantirish quticha ustida katta harflar bilan yozilgan. Demak, yetishmayotgan bo'lak ma'lumot emas. Ancha yaxshi ishlaydigan narsa — atrofni o'zgartirish: uyga boshqa yo'ldan qaytish, juma kuni boshqa do'stlar davrasi.

Aslida, o'z o'qishimda ham xuddi shuni sezganman. Iroda menga hech narsa bermadi. Uydan chiqib ketish berdi.

Bu, hech bo'lmasa, shuni ko'rsatadiki, biz odamlarni irodasi zaif deb ayblaymiz, aslida esa asosiy muammo — biz ulardan o'z oshxonasi bilan kurashishni so'raganmiz.

content.titleUz: Muhim haqiqat: C1 nutqi silliq emas
content.bodyUz:
Ko'p o'quvchi shunday o'ylaydi: «C1 degani — hech to'xtamasdan, xatosiz gapirish». Bu **noto'g'ri tasavvur** va u ko'p zarar keltiradi.

Haqiqiy ona tili egasining nutqini yozib olib, transkript qiling — u to'la:
- pauzalar (*well..., I mean...*)
- o'zini tuzatishlar (*it's expensive — well, expensive for a student, anyway*)
- qayta boshlashlar (*the main thing is... actually, no, the main thing is...*)

Baholash mezonida yozilgani: C1 nomzod **«tabiiy ravishda va deyarli harakatsiz o'zini ifodalaydi; qiyinchiliklarni shu qadar silliq aylanib o'tadiki, tinglovchi buni deyarli sezmaydi»**.

E'tibor bering: «qiyinchilik bo'lmaydi» deb yozilmagan. **«Qiyinchilikni aylanib o'tadi»** deb yozilgan. Ya'ni to'xtash xato emas — **jim qolish va o'zbekcha «e-e-e» qilish** xato.

**1. VAQT YUTISH (stalling).** Fikr kerak bo'lganda, jim qolmang — inglizcha to'ldiring.
*«That's a good question, actually — I've not really thought about it in those terms.»*
*«Hmm, let me think about that for a second.»*
Bu iboralar sizga 3-5 soniya beradi va imtihonchiga ravon eshitiladi.

**2. O'ZINI TUZATISH (self-repair).** Xato qilsangiz, to'xtamang — tuzatib davom eting.
*«...he go — sorry, he went...»*
*«It's expensive — well, expensive for a student, anyway.»*
Ikkinchi tur ayniqsa qimmatli: bu grammatik tuzatish emas, **fikrni aniqlashtirish**. C1 belgisi aynan shu.

**3. AYLANIB O'TISH (paraphrase).** So'z esdan chiqsa, uni qidirib jim qolmang — tushuntiring.
*«...that thing you use to — the device that measures how much you've walked, whatever it's called.»*
Bu **muvaffaqiyat**, mag'lubiyat emas. Aloqa uzilmadi.

content.titleUz: Qaysi to'xtash YOMON, qaysi biri yaxshi
content.bodyUz:
**BALL TUSHIRADIGAN to'xtashlar:**
- Jimlik (2 soniyadan uzun, hech qanday tovushsiz)
- Ona tilidagi tovushlar: «e-e-e», «yani», «xo'sh» (o'zbekcha)
- Savolni so'zma-so'z takrorlab vaqt yutish: *«Do I think cities will change... cities will change...»*
- Bir gapni uch marta boshlash va tashlab yuborish

**BALL TUSHIRMAYDIGAN (yoki hatto KO'TARADIGAN) to'xtashlar:**
- Inglizcha to'ldiruvchi: *well, I mean, sort of, you know*
- Tayyor vaqt yutish iborasi: *that's a good question, let me think*
- Fikrni aniqlashtiruvchi tuzatish: *expensive — well, expensive for a student*
- So'zni aylanib o'tish: *the thing you use to...*

**Xulosa:** maqsad to'xtashni yo'q qilish emas — to'xtashni **inglizchalashtirish**. Miyangiz o'ylayotganda, og'zingiz inglizcha ishlab tursin.

Uchta ibora — favqulodda to'plamingiz. Ularni shu darajada yodlang-ki, uyqudan uyg'otsalar ham ayta olasiz:

1. **«That's a good question, actually — I've not thought about it in those terms.»** (5 soniya)
2. **«How can I put this...»** (2 soniya, gap o'rtasida)
3. **«...the thing you use to — you know what I mean.»** (so'z esdan chiqqanda)

Bu uchtasi imtihonda sizni jimlikdan qutqaradi. Ularni HOZIR ovoz chiqarib 10 marta takrorlang — vahima paytida faqat avtomatlashgan narsa ishlaydi.
